title: Henry Cavill is about to take another geek franchise into outer space

 Cinema's proudest nerd is throwing it back with a nostalgic adaptation of Voltron , an '80s cartoon classic By Jack King 15 November 2026 Getty Despite his handsome Hollywood exterior, within Henry Cavill lies one hell of a geek. He's spoken about how he built his own gaming PC from scratch, for one – and he almost missed a phone call about being cast in Man of Steel because he was busy playing World of Warcraft .
 Survey his post-Superman projects, and you'll find a ton of films and shows that scream nerdcore: take fantasy game adaptation The Witcher on Netflix , in which he played legendary monster hunter Geralt of Rivia. He's leading the charge on a splashy Warhammer 40K show over at Prime Video, having been an avid fan of the tabletop game since he was a kid. There's also Highlander on the horizon, a reboot of the '80s fantasy movie that was a cornerstone of many geekier Gen X and Millennial childhoods.
 Suffice to say, he wears his nerddom on his sleeve. And now he can add another nostalgic geekcore throwback to the pile. He's set to play a key role in the upcoming live-action take on Voltron , which began life as a zany cartoon back in the '80s.
 If you're not up to scratch with the Voltron lore, here's the gist of it: the original animated series dropped in 1984, and focused on a team of heroic space explorers who get around in Transformers -esque robots, the most famous of which are basically robotic lions. The title refers to the gigantic mega-mecha Voltron, made up of all the smaller robots combined. If you're reading this and thinking “that sounds extremely Japanese ,” you'll be glad to know that you're onto something – the original Voltron series was based on the anime shows Beast King GoLion and Armored Fleet Dairugger XV .
 A live-action take on Voltron has been in the works for decades, having changed hands across different creative teams and movie studios. And it'll finally arrive on Prime Video next year. Actual story details are firmly under wraps, but we do know they've assembled a killer cast and creative team. Henry Cavill is obviously in there as King Alfor, the creator of Voltron. Sterling K. Brown is set to play Zarkon, the franchise's main evil dude. Rita Ora is set to play Witch Haggar. And newcomer Daniel Quinn-Toye leads the pack as Keith Kogane. (Yes, seriously – this crazy sci-fi movie is led by a hero called Keith.)
 Director Rawson Marshall Thurber – who previously made Dodgeball: A True Underdog Story , insane Dwayne Johnson vehicle Skyscraper and spy comedy Red Notice – has loved Voltron since he was a kid, so fans can rest easy. “I want to be sure that we stay true to the heart and the spirit of Voltron ,” Thurber said in a TikTok video directed at fellow superfans. “In this film, we're gonna be introducing an entirely new generation of pilots, and we've reimagined Voltron for the live-action world.” Even so, the most iconic fan-friendly elements will remain. Promise.
